item.title: ‘I think that’s cowardice’: Dak Prescott calls it ‘weak’ to blame Brian Schottenheimer
item.description: Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys suffered one of their most painful losses in recent memory on Sunday. And with the heat rising on head coach Brian Schottenheimer, Dak Prescott came to his defense. After the Cowboys blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead and lost to the Arizona Cardinals in overtime, Prescott made it clear he isn’t interested in putting the blame on his coach, calling that “cowardice.” Cowboys’ Collapse The Cowboys led the Cardinals 24-10 early in the fourth quarter on Sunday. But Arizona scored 20 points in the final quarter, including a game-tying touchdown with six seconds left. The Cardinals missed the extra point that would have won it in regulation. But the Cowboys went three-and-out in overtime, and Arizona kicked a field goal to win 33-30. The loss dropped Dallas to 3-5 on the season. Schottenheimer has already faced plenty of criticism this season, with Stephen A. Smith ripping him last month after he called himself a great coach. The latest loss has certainly not calmed the criticism, but Jerry Jones said he isn’t planning to make a coaching change during the season. ‘I Think That’s Cowardice’ During his postgame press conference, Prescott called the loss “one of the toughest” of his career. But he wasn’t going to let Schottenheimer take the fall. “It’s all of us,” Prescott said, via the Cowboys’ official website . “Don’t put the blame on one person. Simple as that. I think that’s weak. I think that’s cowardice.” Prescott went on to say that winning and losing involves everyone, from the players to the coaches and support staff. “It’s never just one person’s fault. Even if I go out there and throw a bunch of interceptions, it’s never just truly one person’s fault. And so, don’t take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us and it’s about us backing him up and backing one another up and we’ll have to show it,” Prescott said. Despite the 3-5 record, the Cowboys aren’t out of it. Nobody in the NFC East has run away with the division, and Prescott said that gives him confidence. “At this point, talk is cheap,” Prescott said. “Telling stories is cheap. We’ve got to go write our own story.” We’ll have to see how the team responds from the loss. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and trade deadline acquisitions Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes are all unrestricted free agents. That puts Jed Hoyer in a tough spot. ESPN's Jeff Passan reports the Cubs could shy away from the potentially groundbreaking contract Skubal could secure this winter. "The Chicago Cubs badly want Skubal. item.title: Michigan football sticking with Tommy Carr at QB 'for foreseeable future'
item.description: The Michigan football quarterback carousel has come to a stop. Tommy Carr will start for Michigan (5-3, 2-3 Big Ten) in this weekend's rivalry game against Michigan State (2-6, 0-5) and beyond, coach Kyle Whittingham said at his weekly press conference Monday when he previewed Saturday's matchup (7:30 p.m, Peacock). "Tommy will start this week and for the foreseeable future, unless something changes," Whittingham said. "He played so well, I mean, it's pretty much a given. We haven't had conversation with the team since the game because Sunday's their day off, but we'll cover all that. We'll cover a lot of that ground this morning." Carr comes off the best game of his career and one of the best for a Michigan quarterback in the past three seasons after he completed 22 of 27 passes (81.4%) for 266 yards with one touchdown and no turnovers in U-M's 28-21 win over Rutgers. He was just as effective on the ground, running 12 times for 54 yards and a pair of scores, both of which came in the second half, including a nine-yard scramble on third-and-7 for the game-winning score with 4:24 to play. 'IT'S A DIRTY GAME': Michigan football getting ready for Michigan State rivalry He kept the offense on the field, converting 12 of 16 third downs, and made plays both on time and off schedule. "Liked everything about what he did," Whittingham said. "You talk about QBR, which is an ESPN analytic QB rating that takes into account not just throwing the ball, running the ball, taking sacks, the whole nine yards. He graded out, I think he was 91 or 92, and the top quarterback in the country right now is like 90 or 89. So bottom line is he played a complete game." U-M entered the weekend as the worst passing team in the Power Four conferences, averaging less than 170 yards per game, and Carr exceeded that by nearly 100 full yards. He was 22 of 25 on plays in which he was kept clean, per Pro Football Focus, and handled the blitz well, completing 5 of 6 passes for 81 yards when Rutgers sent extra men. He didn't need the disguise of play-action to get going, completing 14 of 16 passes without the fake-run action for 198 yards, including a seven-yard fade to JJ Buchanan for the first touchdown of the game. He was also 6 of 7 for 105 yards on passes 10 or more yards downfield and picked up 19 total first downs (16 through the air, three on the ground). Michigan has been desperate for consistent play at the quarterback spot and felt it had to move on from former starter Bryce Underwood after he turned the ball over four times in six quarters in the Minnesota game and the first half against Penn State. Carr did commit two giveaways (one fumble, one interception) in a Week 8 loss to Indiana in his first start, but he appeared much more poised in his second start. His performance against Rutgers left little doubt that it was officially his job moving forward. item.title: ‘It Would’ve Been a Great Situation for Him, Wouldn’t It?’ — NFL Legend Revisits Shedeur Sanders’ Missed Chance With Ravens After Lamar Jackson’s Injury
item.description: ‘It Would’ve Been a Great Situation for Him, Wouldn’t It?’ — NFL Legend Revisits Shedeur Sanders’ Missed Chance With Ravens After Lamar Jackson’s Injury Lamar Jackson was back for the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, but the relief was short-lived as the star quarterback picked up another injury, and Baltimore fell 36-10 to the Bills. Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first play, and head coach Jesse Minter later confirmed that the injury will require surgery and send him to injured reserve for at least four games. His backup, Tyler “Snoop” Huntley, stepped in, only to suffer a toe injury of his own in the second quarter, further complicating an already precarious quarterback situation for Baltimore. Shannon Sharpe, however, believes the Ravens may already have missed out on an intriguing solution. On the latest episode of “Nightcap,” Sharpe discussed Baltimore’s depleted quarterback room with Chad “Ochocinco” Johnson and Joe Johnson before revisiting Shedeur Sanders, whom the Ravens reportedly considered drafting in 2025. Shannon Sharpe Points to Shedeur Sanders’ Missed Opportunity “Hey, you think Snoop would be back next week or no?” Ochocinco asked Sharpe. The three-time Super Bowl winner was not optimistic. “No, I doubt it. I doubt it, Ocho. He might be done for the year… That toe, Ocho, that toe bent.” Ochocinco then brought up how slowly turf toe heals, and Sharpe said he knew exactly how long it takes. Then Sharpe circled back to his original thought. “I know a guy that’d been a great situation for,” he started, before Johnson cut in. “Oh, you talking about 2,” Ochocinco said, referring to Sanders and his jersey number. Sharpe confirmed it. “It would’ve been a great situation for him, wouldn’t it?” he said. Sharpe’s comment carried added significance because Sanders reportedly had the opportunity to become a Raven in the 2025 NFL Draft. Baltimore planned to select him with the No. 141 overall pick in the fifth round, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, but Sanders let the team know that he did not want to join a roster with Jackson, where his path to playing time would have been blocked. item.description: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images Kyle Larson sits on the brink of a historic third NASCAR Cup Series title with a commanding 67-point lead. Per Yahoo Sports , the Hendrick Motorsports driver only needs to score nine points at the Homestead-Miami Speedway finale to officially secure the championship. This margin is so large that he does not even need to win the race or lead any laps to take the trophy home. The virtual world is preparing to mirror this real-world drama with the iRacing Homestead Championship Special Event. This week’s sim race covers 400 miles, or 267 laps, on the same track where real drivers will fight for the crown. According to iRacing, the event features dynamic weather and both fixed and open setup options to test driver skill. The Math Makes It Hard For Challengers Christopher Bell and Denny Hamlin face a nearly impossible task to catch Larson before the checkered flag falls. Bell sits in second place but trails by 67 points, while Hamlin is 70 points behind the leader. Per Yahoo Sports, even if Bell scores the maximum 76 points available in the race, Larson would still win the title by reaching that nine-point threshold. This means Larson can finish 28th or better without earning a single stage point and still lock up the championship. The pressure is entirely on his rivals to hope for a mechanical failure or a crash for the No. 5 Chevrolet. Bell finished 10th at Martinsville and Hamlin came in sixth, but neither could close the gap enough to change the odds. William Byron won the Xfinity 500 at Martinsville to jump to ninth in the standings, but he is not in the championship hunt. item.title: Former Penn State wrestling star Levi Haines wins first world title
item.description: Former Penn State wrestling star Levi Haines is a world champion. Could the Biglerville High grade and two-time NCAA individual champ become a Nittany Lion again? Haines won his first world title Sunday in Kazakhstan as part of a stunning display of success by Penn State-affiliated wrestlers at the World Wrestling Championships. Haines won one of three golds and six medals, overall, by Nittany Lion Wrestling Club members in the penultimate (non-Olympic year) freestyle tournament. Haines won his first world title in the 79 kilogram weight class after placing second last season. NLWC members Kyle Snyder (97 kg) and Kyle Dake (86 kg) each won their fifth world titles. PSU sophomore wrestler Marcus Blaze medaled for the first time on the senior world level with a bronze at 61 kg. Former Penn State wrestler Zain Retherford also won bronze at 70 kg. It was a career-defining performance for Haines, who defeated Iran's Mohammad Nokhodilarimi, 4-3, with a winning takedown in the final two minutes. Haines won three decisive matches to open his world wrestling championships run before surviving a 3-3 semifinals finish with Mongolia's Suldkhuu Olonbayar, winning on criteria. What's next for Penn State wrestling's Levi Haines? Haines now remains in limbo following his world title. The rare four-time Big Ten champion continues to wait on whether he will be able to seek a fifth season of eligibility for the Nittany Lions . He's among thousands of former college athletes awaiting a decision in an antitrust lawsuit against the NCAA to determine their eligibility status for the 2026-27 season. Haines is taking classes at Penn State and wishes to compete for a third NCAA title, according to Penn State coach Cael Sanderson , though there's no timeline for the lawsuit ruling. Sanderson recently said Haines is prepared to re-join the Lions' lineup if eligible. "If he gets the call back to folkstyle, he's been wrestling folkstyle his whole life, so he'll be good to go," Sanderson said. The Lions open their dual meet season Nov. 12 against Bloomsburg in Rec Hall. They're riding an 86-match win streak as they begin pursuing their sixth straight NCAA team title. But the group still had Drake Maye, and that proved to be enough to mount a comeback. “You want to be a great quarterback in the National Football League, there’s not a whole lot of excuses,” head coach Mike Vrabel said post-game. “You go out there and you find ways to win for your football team. He finished the final two quarters 9-of-10 for 146 yards, with three total touchdowns and a perfect 158.3 passer rating. As Vrabel noted, it was the kind of performance expected from an elite quarterback. item.description: Brittany Mahomes, Patrick Mahomes Credit: Grant Halverson/Getty; Matthew Stockman/Getty NEED TO KNOW Brittany Mahomes is sharing her opinion about how the Chiefs-Broncos game ended The wife of Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes criticized a key call late in the game The Chiefs were called for a false start, negating what would have been a game-winning touchdown and sending them back five yards Brittany Mahomes is taking offense about an officiating call that resulted in a Kansas City Chiefs loss on Sunday, Nov. 1. “You can’t tell me you call that on a game winning TD,” Mahomes, 31, wrote in a post to her Instagram Stories. “Oh wait yeah I can cause it’s us.” She continued, “That’s the weakest call I have ever seen. You can’t tell me otherwise.” The call in question involved her husband Patrick Mahomes , who was moments away from leading the team to a win over the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. But refs called a false start on Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore, just before Mahomes hit Rashee Rice with what would have been the game-winning touchdown pass with four seconds left on the clock. Credit: Brittany Mahomes/Instagram The score was wiped away and the team was backed up five yards — all of which culminated in a clunky play in which the quarterback was sacked by Malcolm Roach and time expired. The Chiefs blew an 11-point fourth quarter lead and lost, 28-24, giving the Broncos the top spot in the division. After the game, Chiefs coach Andy Reid backed up Brittany’s assessment. “I didn’t see it,” Reid told reporters about the call. “That’s one man’s opinion. I just didn’t see it. I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see [a] false start.” The Chiefs now sport a 5-2 record after consecutive losses, having lost to Seattle the week before. Brittany, who has a longstanding practice of defending her husband’s team, called out commentators earlier this season in the Chiefs’ first matchup against the Broncos. item.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick (right) and midfielder Kobbie Mainoo speak to the media before the Champions League match against Roma [Getty Images] Michael Carrick accepts it might sound "crazy" but the beleaguered Manchester United boss says he is looking forward to the Champions League showdown with Roma at Old Trafford. United go into Tuesday's game without a win in nine matches in all competitions. It is their worst run since 1988-89. They have not gone 10 without a win in a single campaign since 1977-78 and there is a growing feeling Carrick will lose his job during the forthcoming international break. Roma's only defeat so far this season was at home to Real Madrid in the Champions League last month, when they led 3-1 with seven minutes left. United are 17th in the Premier League and after defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como have slumped to 21st in the Champions League table after three games, with only the top 24 making it through. It is a bleak backdrop, but rather than fret over what lies ahead, Carrick is viewing it as a chance to change the narrative of the season. "You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but genuinely, I really can't wait for the game," said Carrick. "I'm really looking forward to it. "Listen, I can't look into the future, you never know what's going to happen. That doesn't change the way I feel. Whatever happens is going to happen in whatever direction it goes in, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow." Carrick watched over a lively open session of pre-match training at Carrington. item.title: What was Kimi Antonelli’s best moment of his F1 title-winning campaign? Our writers have their say
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli ’s record-breaking Formula 1 world championship triumph was highlighted by many superb performances. But which one was his best? Antonelli duly wrapped up his maiden F1 crown in Mexico with four rounds to spare – becoming the youngest-ever world champion in the process. Our writers have picked out the moments they believe turned the Italian from a contender into a world champion in waiting. Melbourne crash response offered first glimpse of new Kimi – Filip Cleeren Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes It may sound odd to pick one of Antonelli's few defeats against Russell, but his runner-up spot to the Briton at the season opener in Melbourne showed me the first tranche of evidence that the Antonelli who had rocked up Australia wasn't the same insecure rookie who had struggled through spells of 2025. The Albert Park weekend was actually one of Antonelli's more challenging weekends, suffering a heavy 25G crash in FP3 that looked set to derail his weekend. It may have done a year prior, but this time the young Italian stayed cool and collected. And as Mercedes was able to pull off a full rebuild just in time for qualifying, Antonelli was able to shake off the incident and take second on the grid behind Russell despite not being able to finetune the car's set-up. In the race Antonelli then suffered from a poor getaway with no battery power as he was swamped and dropped to sixth, but Mercedes' pace advantage was thus that he was able to make a controlled recovery to second. "If something like that had happened to me last year, the rest of the weekend would probably have been very compromised," Antonelli reflected in Austin. "When you have one year of experience, one full year in Formula 1, you come back the next year and you just feel better. Things happen a bit more easily, let's say, also because you're not forcing them to happen as much. "I kind of took a step back in that regard and just tried to focus on the important things and enjoy the process as much as possible. Definitely, mentally I've been in a much happier place this year compared to last season. And especially when you've been working with the same group of people for one year, going into year two is a big difference as well. You know how to move on together as a team, especially from difficult situations." Canadian GP - Antonelli's real statement drive – Ewan Gale Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes By the time F1 had rocked up to the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve, Antonelli had already proven that he possesses some of the traits needed to be successful. Yet this was the first real ding-dong battle we had seen between the Italian and an adversary that meant something. Fighting for the lead with Russell throughout the first half of the race, we saw that Antonelli was not going to be a pushover for his more experienced team-mate in the race for the title.

item.title: Stat of the Day: Mercedes Needs Only a 3-Point Edge on Ferrari in Brazil to Clinch the Constructors’ Title
item.description: Photo by Jonathan Borba on Pexels.com Mercedes leads Ferrari 630 points to 504 with four Formula 1 rounds left. That 126-point gap looks like a runaway, and it is. The number that matters this week is smaller: three . That is how many points more than Ferrari Mercedes must score in the São Paulo Grand Prix to lock up the constructors’ championship at Interlagos. The math behind the stat A team can score a maximum of 43 points in a grand prix: 25 for a win and 18 for second place. There are no sprint races left, because all six 2026 sprint weekends (Shanghai, Miami, Montréal, Silverstone, Zandvoort and Singapore) are done. The remaining rounds are São Paulo (November 6-8), Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Once Brazil is over, three races will remain, so Ferrari’s ceiling is 3 x 43 = 129 points. If Mercedes leaves Interlagos 129 or more points clear, Ferrari cannot pass it. From a 126-point lead, Mercedes only needs to outscore Ferrari by three. A tie on points would also go to Mercedes on wins, which it leads 12 to 2 this year. What it reveals competitively Three points is a small ask. Mercedes has averaged about 33.2 points per round against Ferrari’s 26.5, a margin of roughly 6.6 per race. The target for Brazil is less than half of its normal edge. For Ferrari to stop the clinch it would need to beat Mercedes by four or more in a single non-sprint race, which in practice means a near-perfect Sunday with Mercedes stumbling at the same time. The split inside the points explains why. Mercedes’ 630 is Kimi Antonelli’s 380 plus George Russell’s 250. Ferrari’s 504 is Lewis Hamilton’s 259 plus Charles Leclerc’s 245. Russell and the Ferrari pair are within a few points of one another; Antonelli is the whole gap . He has won nine of Mercedes’ 12 races, while Ferrari has taken just two wins between its drivers. We broke down his title run in our earlier look at his points lead and his one-stop win in Austin . Photo by Jonathan Borba on Pexels.com Why the clinch matters beyond the trophy The constructors’ standings are where the money is. Final positions set the share of Formula 1’s prize fund, which we explained in how the constructors’ championship determines prize money . Mercedes had already been in the frame to take both crowns, as covered in Mercedes Can Win Both F1 Titles in Mexico City . Antonelli’s drivers’ title is secured, so Brazil is now about whether the team side can be closed out with three races still to run. What to watch in Brazil Ferrari’s one-two ceiling: only a Hamilton-Leclerc double podium combined with a Mercedes weak day keeps the title alive past Interlagos. Russell’s Sunday: Antonelli will score, so Russell’s finish decides whether Mercedes gets there comfortably. The fallback dates: if Brazil does not do it, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi each cut Ferrari’s maximum by another 43. (Photo by Gregory Fisher/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Everybody loves the big-name acquisition, but sometimes, the small, unheralded move that pays dividends can be a real difference maker for a ballclub. On February 6, 2016, the Yankees made one such move, signing minor league free agent Jonathan Loáisiga after he was cut by the San Francisco Giants, as they sought to add pitching depth to the farm system during a transitory period in the organization’s history. The man who would come to be known as “Johnny Lasagna” would go on to fill a critical role in the Yankees’ bullpen during the 2021 season, before injuries ultimately robbed him derailed his Yankees career. Jonathan Stanley Loáisiga Estrada Born: November 2, 1994 (Managua, Nicaragua) Yankees Tenure: 2018-2025 Born and raised in Nicaragua, Loáisiga signed as an international amateur free agent with the San Francisco Giants on September 23, 2012. He made his professional debut the following season, going on to make 13 appearances with the DSL Giants. Although his performance was encouraging — he had just a 2.75 ERA and 1.107 WHIP in that span — his Giants career was effectively over after that; injuries robbed him of the entire 2014 and 2015 seasons, and as a result, the Giants cut him loose. As noted above, Loáisiga signed with the Yankees that winter, and was assigned to Single-A Charleston (the Yankees cut ties with them during the 2020-2021 restructuring, and they are now a member of the Rays family). Immediately, the injury woes followed the young right-hander: just 2.1 innings into his first start he tore his UCL and underwent Tommy John surgery. Unlike the Giants, though, the Yankees were willing to be patient, and added him to the 40-man roster in 2017 in order to protect him from the Rule 5 Draft (something they did not do with Garrett Whitlock a few years later). When he returned to the mound with the GCL Yankees that summer, Loáisiga rewarded that faith. item.title: Jerry Koosman, dead at 83
item.description: NEW YORK, NY - UNKNOWN: Jerry Koosman #36 of the New York Mets poses for a photo with Jerry Koosmans Big Bite Fan Club prior to a National League game on an unknown date at Shea Stadium in the Queens borough of New York City. (Photo by Louis Requena/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Yesterday, the baseball world learned of the passing of Jerry Koosman, a member of both the 1969 World Champion and 1973 National League Champion New York Mets, at 83 year old. Koosman, a member of the Mets Hall of Fame and whose number 36 is retired by the Mets, is one of the most identifiable Mets from their first golden era. Born in Appleton, Minnesota, the left-hander was discovered while in the military, and the Mets signed him one his service was over. He made his big league debut in 1967, but joined the Mets full time in 1968, going 19-12 with a 2.08 ERA and 178 strikeouts in 263.2 innings. Koosman finished second to Johnny Bench in the Rookie of the Year voting. In 1969, Koosman had another fantastic season, and won two games in the ‘69 World Series, pitching 17 and two-thirds innings over two games, and was awarded the ball Cleon Jones caught for the final out of the game. Koosman continued to be the Mets’ number two starter behind Tom Seaver, and he had a number of very good seasons as Met, including winning 21 games in 1976 and coming in second in the Cy Young voting in 1976. After the Mets’ terrible 1978 season, Koosman requested a trade and was traded to the Twins in exchange for Greg Field and, as a player to be named later, fellow Mets legend Jesse Orosco. Over his 12 year Mets career, Koosman put up a 3.07, with a 140-137 record. He was an All-Star in 1968 and 1969. After a fantastic year in 1979 for the Twins, Koosman’s career never quite hit those high marks again. After two and a half seasons with the Twins, two and a half for the White Sox, and two for the Phillies, Koosman retured after the 1985 season. He ended his career with 53.6 bWAR. Koosman has the third most pitching wins in Mets history (140), behind teammate Seaver and Dwight Gooden. The Mets inducted him into their Hall of Fame in 1989 and retired his number in 2021. He was just the third Met player to have his number retired. Koosman is survived by three children and four grandchildren.

item.title: Should the Saints be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline?
item.description: The season for the New Orleans Saints has not gone as the organization had planned so far, and coming off a bye week, the Saints are in a very precarious situation. As the division stands right now, the Saints are only one game out of first place. Every other team has three wins, with the Panthers, who have already had their bye week, sitting at four losses while the rest of the division has five. This puts the Saints in a difficult situation. Do they make a move at the trade deadline to try to go all in and win the division, or do they punt on the 2026 season because of the systemic issues and the need to acquire more young talent on cheap contracts for the long-term challenges ahead? Looking at the roster as it stands right now, if the Saints wanted to bring in some players to help them win, they would have to spend future draft capital on the defensive side of the ball. The Saints spent the entire offseason ignoring some major issues on defense, especially their inability to stop the run. They would have to start there, focusing on the line of scrimmage. The first player to explore would be Grover Stewart, the interior defensive tackle for the Colts. Stewart is one of the best run-stuffing tackles in the league. During his NFL career, he has recorded over 400 total tackles and 13 sacks. The issue with Stewart is that he has now been in the league for nine years. Do you feel comfortable with the Saints sending draft capital in exchange for a veteran who has been in the league this long? Other options include Daron Payne of the Commanders, an eight-year veteran who can defend the run and add valuable interior pass-rushing ability, with 38 sacks over his career, and Dalvin Tomlinson. Tomlinson is not as accomplished as Payne and Stewart, but he is a player known for his play and durability. He has not missed a start over his nine-year career, and on a team that struggles with health issues, this would be an immediate upgrade. The Saints could also look at linebackers like Cody Barton of the Titans and Daiyan Henley of the Chargers. But at this point, the Saints should not be comfortable giving up draft capital in a season like this one. This is not a team that is just a single player away from making a run. It’s one thing to consider going on a championship run with the playoffs in sight, but this team is trying to make a run to win a poor division. This is a team trying to make a run to win eight or nine games. This is not an acceptable position to be in when it comes to trading away future assets just to finish a season with fewer than double-digit wins. As the trade deadline approaches, the Saints may want to consider trading players to acquire more assets. Austin Simmons lined up in the gun, with Jamal Roberts aligned to his left. Simmons simply could’ve just handed it off to Roberts. But with the play clock going under 15 seconds, Simmons sprinted under center, with Roberts aligned off the left tackle. DeMarion Fowlkes finished his motion by aligning the offset of Jordon Harris. A quarterback sneak with a 6-foot-4 Simmons is another option, but instead, it’s Fowlkes taking the ball on a jet sweep. Believe it or not, the Phillies had real hopes for Otto Kemp heading into 2026. He put up a .786 OPS against left-handed pitching in 2025, roughly 20% above league average, believe it or not. Kemp notably played through a fractured left kneecap and he needed surgery on his shoulder after the 2025 season. He clearly checked the intangible boxes and showed some real ability at the plate. He slugged .411 with a 92 OPS+ as a rookie and did not look incompetent against right-handed pitching most of the time. Dave Dombrowski clearly liked what he saw, insisting he thought Kemp could turn into an everyday player but they settled on the short-side platoon LF spot. He was never a good defender but he wasn’t completely unathletic and should hit lefties. Sounds like a perfectly acceptable platoon partner for Brandon Marsh, right? Nope. It was a disaster. What went right? Kemp made the opening day roster and the Phillies came into the season with him in mind so clearly something went fine in spring training, at least enough so the Phillies could maintain the course. What went wrong? After going 2 for 20 with nine strikeouts, a walk, and a hit-by-pitch, not to mention he was a disaster in left field, Kemp was optioned in the middle of the Phillies 10 game losing streak. Felix Reyes came in his place, hit a home run off Chris Sale but nothing else and would later get optioned. item.title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake beats South Glens Falls for its 4th straight Section 2 Class B field hockey title
item.description: Burnt Hills celebrates after defeating South Glens Falls to win the Section 2 Class B championship on Sunday at Glens Falls High School. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) GLENS FALLS - When Grace Kogut and Katie Lansley were eighth graders on the 2022 Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake field hockey team, their first varsity season ended in devastation. That 2022 season ended the Spartans' run of nine consecutive Section 2 Class B championships. In the years since, Kogut and Lansley have been key contributors for the program, as it's begun a brand new stretch of dominance. On Sunday afternoon, Burnt Hills defeated South Glens Falls 6-1 to secure its fourth straight Class B championship. "A little bit, but I'm very confident in our team," Kogut, now a senior, said on whether she ever gets flashbacks from the championship game loss in 2022, which came against South Glens Falls. "Today we were ok, but there's definitely some bad memories there. "At least for me, I feel like after that loss, we wanted to push to get better. It was heartbreaking and I know we never wanted to feel like that again." In addition to Burnt Hills' four straight Section 2 titles, the Spartans are two-time defending Class B state champions and are set to return to the state tournament looking to defend their crown. "We're really proud of the team to get it up to four. Even though we had so many before and we lost (in 2022), it's really good to see us build it back up," Lansley said. "I think it's the team culture, and we're a family. We carry that on to the field. Every year, the team is so close on and off the field, and I feel like that really carries us." Burnt Hills' Katie Lansley navigates through the South Glens Falls defense during the Section 2 Class B championship game on Sunday at Glens Falls High School. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) Key moment Riley Rodecker got Burnt Hills on the board midway through the first quarter, and the Spartans kept the momentum the rest of the way. The top-seeded Spartans, who received a bye into the title game, scored two goals in the first quarter and two in the second, to take a 4-0 lead into the half against the second-seeded Bulldogs. They added another goal in the third and fourth quarters for a 6-1 victory. "We always tell them, ‘Next game,'" said Burnt Hills coach Kelly Vrooman. "I know we have this game (under control), but we have to look ahead to the next game, to stick to the details and (uphold) the standard we have here." Star of the game A mix of Burnt Hills' senior leaders and youngsters made an impact on the scoreboard on Sunday. While Kogut had two goals and an assist and Lansley had two assists, freshman forward Carah DiCaprio had the standout performance with three goals and an assist. Maeve McCarty punched in the lone goal for South Glens Falls in the third quarter, as she navigated her way down the field for an unassisted score. item.title: Rays decline options on Martinez & Mullins
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 23: Nick Martinez #28 of the Tampa Bay Rays throws a pitch during the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game one of the 2026 World Series at American Family Field on October 23, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Rays have officially parted ways with two veteran players that were integral to the team’s run to the World Series this past season. On Friday, October 30th, the Rays announced that they had declined the mutual options for the 2027 season with RHP Nick Martinez and OF Cedric Mullins. The Rays signed Martinez just prior to Spring Training to a one year, $9M contract with a $20M mutual option for the 2027 season; the Rays paid Martinez a $4M buyout after declining that option. The signing could not have worked out any better for Tampa Bay and Martinez as the veteran hurler delivered one of his best seasons and was named an All-Star for the first time in his career. Overall the 36 year old compiled a 3.10 ERA | 3.96 FIP with a 15.1 K% and league leading 3.6 BB% over a career high, 180 IP. Off the field, Martinez’s leadership within the clubhouse was invaluable as he helped guide a young Rays team to their first postseasom berth since 2023. When the Rays reached the World Series for the third time in franchise history, Nick Martinez received the honor of starting Game One against the Milwaukee Brewers. Early last offseason, the Rays signed the veteran Cedric Mullins to a one year, $7M deal with a $10M mutual option for the 2027 season. The Rays have declined that option and instead paid Mullins a $500K buyout. Mullins wasn’t able to recapture the magic that had made him one of the top players in baseball while with the Baltimore Orioles several years ago. The now 32 year old Mullins had one of the worst offensive seasons in baseball in 2026 and also posted the lowest OBP% among qualifying players in a single-season for the Rays. Overall Mullins hit .205/.284/.344 with 15 HR and 21 SB, registering a 76 wRC+ (4th lowest of 135 players). Mullins did accrue 1.1 fWAR despite his lowly offensive production thanks to plus defense in center field, producing 11 Outs Above Average, which ranked 4th among 54 qualifying outfielders. With the departures of Mullins and Martinez, the Rays will likely be on the hunt for new veteran additions to fill their respective roles on the team.
